subtype: Approach: going along because refusing feels rude [Pitfall]
passage: It was raining hard outside the tuition centre when a man stepped up to Vinita. "Your mother has had an accident. Come with me quickly." Vinita's stomach lurched. Her grandmother's rule rang in her ears: always listen to elders, never be rude. She followed him two lanes, her shoes soaked, though a small voice said, wait. At the corner, Vikas, the paan-shop owner who knew her family, called, "Vinita! Where are you going?" The man walked off fast. Vikas phoned her mother, who answered from home, perfectly well. Vinita was shaking. Later, drying her hair, she wondered why no one had told her that saying no was allowed too.

qa.q: Who called out to Vinita at the corner?
qa.a: Vikas, the paan-shop owner who knew her family, called out.

qa.q: What was Vinita feeling as she followed the man?
qa.a: Frightened for her mother, and torn between the rule to obey elders and a small voice saying wait.

qa.q: What could Vinita do instead if a stranger says her mother is hurt, and why?
qa.a: She could refuse to go, stay near people and ask a trusted adult to phone her mother, because a real emergency can be checked without following a stranger.

qa.q: How does Vikas see the situation at the corner?
qa.a: Vikas sees a child from a family Vikas knows walking off with a stranger, so Vikas steps in and phones her mother.

grounding: A child taught to be polite to elders follows a stranger and is rescued, then sees safety must come before politeness.

subtype: Approach: going along because refusing feels rude [Pitfall]
passage: Lakshmi had been taught to always say "yes, uncle" to elders. So when a man at the school gate said, "Your mother fell down at home. She's hurt. Come with me quickly," her body went cold, and she started walking with him. He walked fast, toward the main road. Halfway down the lane, Tarun sir, the PE teacher, came round the corner on his bicycle. "Lakshmi? Where are you going?" The man turned and hurried away. Tarun sir brought her back inside, stayed beside her, and phoned her mother, who was fine, at home, cooking. He told Lakshmi, "You did nothing wrong. He tricked you." The principal informed the police and all parents that afternoon.

qa.q: Who came round the corner on a bicycle?
How did Lakshmi feel when the man said her mother was hurt?
qa.a: She felt cold with shock and fear, and her wish to be polite and help made her follow.

qa.q: What should Lakshmi do if something like this happens again, and why?
qa.a: Say no, stay inside the gate and go to a teacher to check, because safety matters more than being polite.

qa.q: How does the afternoon look to Tarun sir?
qa.a: Tarun sir is alarmed to see Lakshmi with a stranger and acts fast, bringing her back, calling her mother and reassuring her.

grounding: It shows a child raised to be polite to elders following a stranger who says her mother is hurt, and learning that politeness should not override safety.

subtype: Approach: going along because refusing feels rude [Pitfall]
passage:
"Ishita! Ishita! Where are you going?"
"Vijay bhaiya! This uncle says Mummy's hurt. I have to go."
"Which uncle?"
"He was just here... he's walking away."
"Come back inside the gate. Now. Stand by me."
"But Mummy..."
"I'll call her. Stay here." He dialled. "Aunty? Are you all right? ... Okay. No, she's safe with me."
"Is she hurt?"
"She's at home, cooking. She's fine."
"But I said yes. I couldn't say no to an elder."
"You're not in trouble. It's not your fault. But being safe comes before being polite."
Vijay walked her to the office, and the principal called her parents in that afternoon.

qa.q: What did the man tell Ishita?
How did Ishita feel when she learned her mother was fine?
qa.a: She was confused and upset, and felt she had to say yes because refusing an elder felt rude.

qa.q: What would you advise Ishita for next time?
qa.a: Stay inside the gate and check with a trusted adult before going anywhere, even if the story sounds urgent.

qa.q: How does the moment look to Vijay?
qa.a: Vijay is alarmed and acts calmly and quickly, bringing her back, checking on her mother and reassuring her it isn't her fault.

grounding: It shows a child who follows a stranger because refusing an elder feels rude, and learns that politeness should not override safety.
